source.title: On the Stability of the Jacobian Matrix in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: B. Dadoun; Soufiane Hayou; H. Salam; Mohamed El Amine Seddik; Pierre Youssef

record.file_problem: The full text is present. Some equations and figure content are flattened, and exact plotted values cannot be recovered from the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares initialization settings and reports trained-network test error, addressing initialization and trainability. It does not measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results concern Jacobian norms, not classification error. Figures 8–9 report validation accuracy and loss for pruned networks, but do not report exact values in the text. These outcomes do not measure the training-error claims in the versions. Figure 10 reports test error after convergence and explicitly describes trainability under critical initialization; it bears on V4, but does not establish training-error behavior.
record.test_reason: The study compares initialization variance, weight correlation, and scaling after pruning, and reports empirical trainability across depth. These results bear on V4's trainable-depth component, although they do not measure training speed or training classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish fixed-depth, infinite-width Jacobian-norm universality for suitably rescaled sparse networks and sufficiently weakly correlated Gaussian weights. They emphasize initialization and pruning-specific scaling, while limiting their theory to MLPs and random or magnitude-based pruning.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines initialization effects and Jacobian stability, rather than reproducing the claim's CIFAR classification-error experiments. Its empirical training results use MLPs on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and a sparse or correlated-weight setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization variance and depth affect the reported trainability results. Pruning method and scaling affect Jacobian stability and validation performance; weight correlation affects Jacobian behavior and trainability.

fits_no_version.finding: The universality theorem and Jacobian-only experiments establish spectral-norm behavior under variance matching, sparsity conditions, and weak weight dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed depth and asymptotically large width, suitably rescaled sparse weights and sufficiently weakly correlated Gaussian weights can match the critically initialized iid model's Jacobian norm.

record.problems: The classification results are test or validation measures, not training classification error. Exact plotted values in Figure 10 are not stated in the text. The theoretical results concern fixed-depth, infinite-width limits and the authors say their theory currently applies only to MLPs. The reported empirical studies use small MLPs and a limited set of datasets and settings.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 8–9 report validation accuracy and loss across depth, sparsity, and normalization/scaling conditions for Fashion-MNIST, but exact values are figure-only and these measures do not match a tested claim version's training-error outcome. The Jacobian-only results in Figures 1–4 likewise do not measure training error or the version-specific outcomes. No rows were extracted for those results.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity shortcuts; the stated tanh and Fixup comparisons.
Direct training-speed comparisons; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks; orthogonal convolution kernels and training at 10,000 layers.
Learning rates relative to a curvature-based stability threshold, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no batch normalization for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup. The figures' normalization terminology denotes weight scaling after pruning.

missing.what: Rows for the correlated-initialization comparison: low correlation preserves trainability at large depths, while high correlation prevents it. Record the three correlation settings separately where identifiable; exact test errors are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section 6.3 and Figure 10 right caption: width 256, Fashion-MNIST, SGD learning rate 0.001, 70 epochs

record.verdict_notes: Validation or test performance can bear on V4's trainable-depth component when the authors explicitly interpret the comparisons as trainability results; training classification error is not required by that component. Figures 8–9 therefore bear on V4 despite the record's exclusion rationale, but are already declared in rows_left_out and are not newly missing results. Jacobian stability alone does not establish learning speed or successful optimization. This study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity shortcuts, and the stated residual or special-initialization comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization schemes beyond the tested iid Gaussian variances; orthogonal weights and convolutional networks; training speed and training error are not reported.
Training above the stability limit, loss rise and recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization versus no normalization as a training-speed or learning-rate comparison, and Fixup.

relationships.condition: Width-256 MLPs on Fashion-MNIST with low versus high initial weight correlation
relationships.reason: The Figure 10 right caption states that low correlation preserves trainability at large depths whereas high correlation does not; this verdict rests on text and requires the missing rows.
relationships.display_finding: Low initial weight correlation preserved trainability at large depths, whereas high correlation did not.

relationships.condition: Randomly pruned width-256 MLPs on Fashion-MNIST, with versus without initialization weight scaling
relationships.reason: Section 6.2 explicitly reports improved trainability after scaling, consistent with preserving gradient propagation; Figures 8–9 were declared omitted and provide validation outcomes rather than training error.
relationships.display_finding: Scaling initial weights improved trainability after random pruning.
